answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with transaction-graph clustering: identities that only trade with each other form a tight vine of links, standing out against honest agents whose connections spread widely like a mesa plain. A lone knoll of self-dealing accounts is easy to spot, and the network can quarantine the whole cluster at once. Running a thousand fakes then requires faking a thousand realistic, diverse transaction histories — each one expensive to fabricate — instead of spinning up free identities.
